subsystems.name: Sleep-stage sensing
subsystems.role: detects REM sleep in real time so cues can be timed to it.

subsystems.name: On-device processing
subsystems.role: runs sleep-staging algorithms and decides when to deliver a cue.

subsystems.name: Sensory cueing
subsystems.role: delivers subtle light or sound that can enter a dream.

subsystems.name: Mask and ergonomics
subsystems.role: holds sensors against the scalp and blocks light for comfort.

subsystems.name: Power and connectivity
subsystems.role: keeps the device running overnight and syncs data.

subsystems.name: Companion app
subsystems.role: sets goals, reviews sleep data and adjusts cue intensity.

buildSteps.title: Design the sensor headband
buildSteps.detail: Place dry electrodes at standard positions (e.g. frontal and occipital) and test signal quality through hair and movement.

buildSteps.title: Develop the sleep-staging algorithm
buildSteps.detail: Train software to distinguish REM from other stages using EEG, eye movement and muscle tone, and run it in real time on a low-power chip.

buildSteps.title: Integrate cue delivery
buildSteps.detail: Add LEDs or speakers that produce brief, low-intensity flashes or tones without waking the sleeper.

buildSteps.title: Build the mask
buildSteps.detail: Combine a light-blocking fabric shell with a flexible circuit board, battery and adjustable straps for comfort.

buildSteps.title: Write firmware and app
buildSteps.detail: Link sensors, cueing and Bluetooth so the phone can configure the device and view results.

buildSteps.title: Validate in a sleep lab
buildSteps.detail: Compare the device's REM detection against polysomnography and measure how often cues are delivered at the right moment.

buildSteps.title: Run user studies
buildSteps.detail: Test whether cueing increases lucid dream frequency, and iterate on timing and intensity.

buildSteps.title: Manufacture and certify
buildSteps.detail: Produce units and meet electrical safety and radio regulations for a wearable.

prerequisites.why: they avoid gel but pick up more noise from hair and movement than clinical electrodes.
algorithms exist but accuracy on a single-channel wearable is lower than in a sleep lab.
studies show modest increases in lucid dreams, not a reliable trigger for everyone.
batteries and chips can run a mask for a night.
fabrics and foams already used in sleep masks.

pathway.milestone: consumer masks with timed light or sound cues, often without EEG
closed-loop masks with validated dry EEG that deliver cues only during confirmed REM
pathway.unlocks: higher and more reliable lucid dream rates.

pathway.milestone: clinical trials for nightmare disorder and PTSD
pathway.unlocks: a medical use for targeted dream therapy.

pathway.milestone: targeted dream incubation, where specific content or skills are rehearsed in dreams
pathway.unlocks: applications in learning, creativity and mental health.
